title_ar: الشيخ الددو يحاضر في الحوض الغربي ضمن برنامجه الدعوي في الشرق الموريتاني
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures in Hodh el Gharbi as Part of His Da'wah Programme in Eastern Mauritania
body_ar:
نظمت جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم صباح اليوم - الثلاثاء 12 سبتمبر 2023م - محاضرة في مقاطعة العيون تحدث فيها فضيلة الشيخ عن خصائص المجتمع المسلم وما ينبغي أن يتصف به من أخلاق فاضلة وقيم..
مبينا أن الدين الإسلامي جعل من المجتمع مجتمعا متكافلا لا يظلم فيه أحد، وقد وضع الأسس الكفيلة ببناء المجتمع الإسلامي، فجعل الناس شركاء في ثلاث ( الماء والنار والعشب )..
كما تحدث فضيلته عن الدعوات الغريبة التي أراد أعداء الدين نشرها وتسويقها في المجتمع المسلم؛
مبينا أن كل تلك الدعوات باطلة، ومن الضلال ترويجها، والأخذ بها ضاربا المثل بالصراع الذي تقوده الحركة النسوية ضد القوامة وكيان الأسرة محذرا من تلك الأفكار الهدامة، والمعتقدات الشاذة.
وقد نصح فضيلته التجار بمراعاة الحلال، والحذر من الحرام، والصدق في البيع، وإخلاص النية لله وحده في ذلك كله؛
كما تحدث عن حقوق الجار وأن المسلم متحضر بذاته كما حث على خلق التعاون وبذل المعروف بين المسلمين.
وتأتي هذه المحاضرة ضمن البرنامج الدعوي لفضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو الذي أطلقته الجمعية مساء السبت 09 سبتمبر الجاري من مدينة اغشوركيت بمقاطعة ألاك عاصمة ولاية البراكنة
ويتضمن البرنامج مجموعة من المحاضرات في كل من الحوضين والعصابة ولبراكنة
وقد تم منها حتى الآن محاضرات كل من اغشوركيت وبوخزامة والنعمة وتنبدغة ولعيون..
وقد ألقى فضيلته ظهر اليوم محاضرة بالجامع الكبير بمقاطعة الطينطان تحدث فيها عن مسؤولية المسلم تجاه دينه مبينا نماذج من محبة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وما يجب أن يكون عليه المسلمون تجاهه.
body_en:
This morning, Tuesday 12 September 2023, the al-Mustaqbal Association for Da'wah, Culture and Education organised a lecture in the district of Aioun, in which His Eminence the Sheikh spoke about the characteristics of the Muslim society and the virtuous character and values by which it ought to be marked..
explaining that the religion of Islam made of society a society of mutual support in which no one is wronged, and that it laid down the foundations that guarantee the building of the Islamic society, making people partners in three things (water, fire and pasture)..
His Eminence also spoke about the strange calls that the enemies of religion have wanted to spread and to market within Muslim society;
explaining that all those calls are void (bāṭil), that promoting them is part of going astray, and that so is taking them up — giving as an example the struggle led by the feminist movement against the husband's stewardship (qiwāmah) and against the entity of the family, and warning against those destructive ideas and aberrant beliefs.
His Eminence counselled the traders to have regard to what is lawful, to beware of what is forbidden (ḥarām), to be truthful in selling, and to keep their intention sincere to God alone in all of that;
He also spoke about the rights of the neighbour, and that the Muslim is civilised in himself; and he urged the character of cooperation and the giving of kindness among the Muslims.
This lecture comes within the da'wah programme of His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, which the Association launched on the evening of Saturday 9 September of this month from the town of Aghchorguitt in the district of Aleg, capital of the region of Brakna.
The programme includes a set of lectures in each of the two Hodhs, Assaba and Brakna.
Of these there have so far taken place the lectures at Aghchorguitt, Boukhzama, Néma, Timbedra and Aioun..
At midday today His Eminence delivered a lecture at the great congregational mosque in the district of Tintane, in which he spoke about the Muslim's responsibility towards his religion, setting out examples of love for the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, and of what the Muslims ought to be towards him.

flags.arabic: مبينا أن كل تلك الدعوات باطلة
flags.context: the news desk's summary of what the Sheikh said about the ideas he was warning against
options: explaining that all those calls are void (bāṭil)
explaining that all those calls are false
explaining that all those calls are invalid
flags.note: The glossary fixes bāṭil as 'void' because in fiqh it concerns the validity of an act or contract. Here the word is applied not to a contract but to ideas, where ordinary Arabic bāṭil means false or baseless. Rendering it 'void' reads oddly and 'invalid' imports the contracts sense. The recommendation therefore departs from the glossary for this occurrence; the glossary rendering has been kept in the English with the term bracketed so the departure is visible, and a reviewer should settle which stands.

flags.arabic: الصراع الذي تقوده الحركة النسوية ضد القوامة وكيان الأسرة
flags.context: the example the report says the Sheikh gave
options: the struggle led by the feminist movement against the husband's stewardship (qiwāmah) and against the entity of the family
the conflict the feminist movement is waging against male authority and the institution of the family
the campaign of feminism against qiwāmah and the family unit
flags.note: qiwāmah is not in the glossary. It denotes the husband's responsibility for and authority over the household under Qur'an 4:34, and there is no settled English equivalent; 'male authority' overstates and 'maintenance' understates. Left as 'the husband's stewardship' with the term bracketed. Needed as a glossary addition.

translator_notes: A news report by the site's news desk summarising lectures. The positions described are the desk's account of what the Sheikh said, not his own wording, and none of it is a fatwa.
The doubled full stops (..) at several line ends are in the source and have been preserved in body_ar and mirrored in body_en rather than normalised.

شركاء في ثلاث ( الماء والنار والعشب ) alludes to a well-known hadith on the three things people share in. The report neither quotes it as a hadith nor names a narrator or collection, so no attribution and no grading has been supplied.
Place names in the Mauritanian official spellings: Aioun, Aghchorguitt, Aleg, Brakna, Assaba, Néma, Timbedra, Tintane. الحوضين is 'the two Hodhs' — Hodh ech Chargui and Hodh el Gharbi.
editorial_review_reasons: The record reports the Sheikh describing the feminist movement's aims as void and as 'destructive ideas and aberrant beliefs'. Rendered faithfully, as required, the passage reads in English as a direct attack on a named social movement, and the words 'aberrant' and 'destructive' carry more force in English than the Arabic does in a news summary. Published without its context this is a reputational exposure for Ummah Collective. Nothing has been softened; the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.
